text:
maria: Heads-up: seeing ~9% tail regression on host-side for streaming gRPC after the kernel-selector tweak. p99 for small streaming requests jumped from ~120ms -> 132ms. Profiling attached below.

kevin: Is that prod or a canary run?

maria: Prod samples from us-west region, spike started at 11:12. Quick summary from perf sample (aggregated):
```
parse_ns: 43ms
tokenize_ns: 12ms
writev_syscalls: 6 calls per request
kv_lookup_ns: 1ms
```
Root cause looks concentrated in parse_state::consume + syscall churn on writev.

nate: That timing smells like the kernel selector fallback introduced more copy/pass-throughs. We started preferring compatibility kernels when model_shape mismatch occurs which can lose inplace tokenize vector path.

jisoo: Also saw increased fragmentation on the http2/gRPC layer. If writev isn't coalescing chunks at the host-proxy boundary we amplify syscalls. Could be two independent regressions stacked.

kevin: I ran a small staging microbench: 512B chunk frames vs 4KB coalesced reduces syscalls ~4x and reduces parse latency. Suggest enabling stream-coalesce with a tiny flush window (2ms) in host-proxy as a quick mitigation.

maria: Can we try a quick toggle? Patch suggestion: set `--stream-coalesce-ms=2` and enable `host.tokenize.inplace=true` to prefer the old fast path. Command to test locally: `NODE_ENV=staging ./bin/host-proxy --stream-coalesce-ms=2 --tokenize-inplace`

deploy-bot: deploy queued: host-proxy-staging #1876 (started)

nate: We should also guard kernel selector: prefer vectorized tokenizer when `seq_len < 256 && model_family == "llama"` (or other CPU-friendly families). That reduces fallback churn for short prompts.

jisoo: I'll check kvcache metrics for eviction spikes — I suspect parse reassembly flushes are causing repeated prefix evictions. Look at `kvcache.evictions_total` and `kvcache.prefetch_hits` over the window.

maria: If the coalesce patch drops syscalls, we should see p99 return to baseline in staging. If not, we revert the kernel-selector change. Also: add an e2e that streams 1KB frames to catch this class of regression automatically.

kevin: I'll run a 30-min synthetic against staging and post the flame.

jisoo: Flame after coalesce + inplace tokenization (staging):
```
parse_ns: 28ms
tokenize_ns: 9ms
writev_syscalls: 1-2 per request
p99: 122ms
```
Looks promising. I'll open a small PR with the coalesce toggle + kernel selector guard and include a perf microbench that asserts syscalls < 3 for typical 1-2KB streams.

maria: Great. Please also add a short regression test in the perf-runbook and @eng-sre so we can monitor a rollback signal. /cc @eng-sre

kevin: :thumbsup: filing the PR and the bench now.

maria: Thanks all — once PR lands we'll run canary and if stable promote to prod.
